# pantechdynamics_bucket (Resource)

An S3-compatible object storage bucket. Object storage is in closed beta: an organization outside it is refused with OBJECT_STORAGE_NOT_ENABLED. Storage is billed per GiB stored, measured hourly; data out and requests are free during the beta. Reach the bucket with any S3 tool at `endpoint`, using a pantechdynamics_object_storage_key. **Destroying a bucket that holds objects fails unless force_destroy is true, which deletes them.**

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A bucket for application uploads, limited to 100 GiB, keeping earlier
# versions of objects, with one prefix anyone may read. Storage is billed per
# GiB stored, measured hourly. Object storage is in closed beta.
resource "pantechdynamics_bucket" "uploads" {
  name            = "acme-app-uploads"
  quota_bytes     = 100 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024
  versioning      = true
  public_prefixes = ["public/"]

  # Destroying a bucket that holds objects fails unless this is true, which
  # deletes the objects with it.
  force_destroy = false
}

output "uploads_endpoint" {
  value = pantechdynamics_bucket.uploads.endpoint
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Bucket name: 3 to 63 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit. Names are shared by every customer, so it must not be taken. Changing it replaces the bucket.

### Optional

- `force_destroy` (Boolean) When true, destroying the bucket deletes every object in it. When false (the default) a bucket that holds objects cannot be destroyed. Terraform only; not sent to the API until destroy.
- `object_lock` (Boolean) Allow retention on objects. Defaults to false. It cannot be turned off, so changing it replaces the bucket.
- `public_prefixes` (Set of String) Key prefixes anyone may read without a key, such as "public/". Leave it out for a wholly private bucket. Changes in place.
- `quota_bytes` (Number) Size limit in bytes; writes beyond it are refused. 0 (the default) is no limit. Changes in place.
- `region` (String) Region code, such as "af-abj". Leave it out for the default region. Changing it replaces the bucket.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `versioning` (Boolean) Keep earlier versions of objects. Defaults to false. Changes in place; turning it off suspends versioning and keeps the versions already stored.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the bucket was created, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second.
- `endpoint` (String) The S3 endpoint URL for this bucket's region.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the bucket, starting with bkt_.
- `state` (String) "provisioning", "active", "updating", "deleting", "failed" or "unknown".

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A bucket is imported by its id or by its name. force_destroy starts false.
terraform import pantechdynamics_bucket.uploads bkt_06ggf6abcdefghjkmnpqrstvw
terraform import pantechdynamics_bucket.uploads acme-app-uploads
```
